evidence.quote: I want an outside read on the plan before it goes to the board, and you've seen more of these than anyone I can get on a call.

observations.why: Tanya explicitly invites external consultation based on Tony's demonstrated expert experience across prior programmes.

evidence.quote: I've watched three of these programmes up close. The two that went big-bang both went backwards — not failed, went backwards, six months of unpicking. The one that went sequentially was boring and finished.

observations.why: Tony asserts expert authority and rational persuasion by citing empirical comparative outcomes from his direct observation of past implementations.

evidence.quote: Write down now, while you're calm, why you chose sequential. When they come at you in month four you want the reasons in your own handwriting, not reconstructed under pressure.

observations.why: Tony provides tactical advisory instruction based on predicting organizational pressure dynamics.

evidence.quote: somebody who isn't the programme manager owns the gate, because the programme manager has a date.

observations.why: Tony argues for structural governance separation of powers, positioning gate ownership outside conflicting schedule delivery authority.

evidence.quote: I'll take that to the board as the open item rather than wait for them to find it.

observations.why: Tanya plans an upward influence move by controlling the disclosure and framing of program vulnerabilities before governance identifies them.
